title: EPUB vs MOBI vs PDF: Which Format Should You Use for KDP?
excerpt: MOBI is retired, PDF is print-only, and EPUB is what KDP wants. Here is a plain-English breakdown of the three ebook formats and which one to upload to Amazon.
meta_title: EPUB vs MOBI vs PDF: Which Format for KDP? | BookKraft AI
meta_description: Confused by EPUB, MOBI, and PDF for Amazon KDP? Learn which ebook format to upload, why MOBI is retired, and when PDF still makes sense for print.
feature_image_alt: Three ebook file format icons compared side by side
html:
If you are about to publish on Amazon KDP, you have probably seen three file formats mentioned: EPUB, MOBI, and PDF. They are not interchangeable, and choosing the wrong one leads to rejected uploads or a book that looks broken on a phone. This guide explains what each format is for and which one to actually upload.

The short answer

For a Kindle ebook on KDP, upload an EPUB. MOBI is retired and no longer accepted for new uploads. PDF is for print books and fixed-layout titles, not standard reflowable ebooks. If you only remember one thing, remember: reflowable ebook means EPUB.

EPUB: the modern ebook standard

EPUB is the open standard used by nearly every ebook retailer — Amazon, Apple Books, Kobo, Google Play, and Barnes & Noble. It is a reflowable format, which means the text adapts to the reader's screen, font size, and line spacing. A reader on a small phone and a reader on a large tablet each get text sized for their device.

KDP now accepts EPUB directly and converts it internally to the Kindle format delivered to devices. Because EPUB is what every other store wants too, a single clean EPUB is the most portable file you can produce. Before uploading, run it through the free EPUB Validator to catch structural errors that cause rejection. If your file needs structural repairs, the EPUB Formatter fixes common manifest and navigation issues.

MOBI: the retired Amazon format

MOBI was Amazon's original ebook format, later paired with the KF8/AZW3 formats. For years, authors converted their books to MOBI to upload to KDP. That era is over. Amazon retired MOBI for new uploads — the Kindle Previewer no longer exports it, and Send to Kindle stopped accepting it.

If you have an old MOBI file from a previous edition, don't upload it. Convert your source manuscript to a fresh EPUB instead. A MOBI built years ago often carries outdated structure that a modern EPUB avoids entirely. If you are cleaning up an older manuscript in the process, the Kindle Format Fixer clears the smart-quote, dash, and encoding artifacts that Word exports leave behind.

PDF: print-only, with one exception

PDF is a fixed-layout format. Every page is locked to a specific size, exactly like a sheet of paper. That is perfect for a print book, where the page never changes — and PDF is exactly what KDP Print and IngramSpark want for paperback and hardcover interiors and covers.

It is a poor choice for a reflowable ebook. On a phone, a PDF page designed for a 6×9 inch print book shrinks until the text is unreadable, and the reader has to pinch and pan on every page. There is no font-size control and no reflow.

The one exception is a fixed-layout ebook — a cookbook, a children's picture book, or a graphic-heavy title where the exact layout matters. Those use a special fixed-layout EPUB, not a plain PDF, but the underlying idea of a locked page is similar.

Which format for which job

  • Kindle ebook (novel, non-fiction, most books): EPUB.
  • Other stores (Apple, Kobo, Google Play): the same EPUB.
  • Paperback or hardcover interior: print-ready PDF.
  • Print cover: full-wrap PDF in CMYK.
  • Cookbook or picture book: fixed-layout EPUB.
  • Old MOBI file: don't use it — export a new EPUB.

Get your EPUB right the first time

Because EPUB does nearly all the work, the real task is producing a clean one. Most rejections come from structural problems inside the file — missing navigation, broken manifest references, or metadata gaps — not from the format choice itself.

Validate before you upload with the EPUB Validator, and if you are starting from a Word document, see our EPUB formatting guide for the full manuscript-to-EPUB workflow. Getting the EPUB right once means one file that uploads cleanly to every store.
